speaker_role: independent counselor (Brooke, SupertutorTV, former Stanford admissions volunteer; also SAT/ACT tutor)
commercial_incentive: Yes - repeatedly promotes her SAT/ACT prep courses and math books via supertutortv.com and Amazon
key_insights: Recommenders should be chosen so that no two parts of the application overlap - each essay/letter should reveal a different facet of the applicant
Colleges want recommenders to speak specifically to academic performance in ways that complement, not duplicate, the rest of the application
Pick recommenders who have a distinctive personal story about you, not necessarily the teacher you like most
Consider choosing a recommender in the subject area relevant to your intended major (e.g., a math/science teacher for engineering applicants)
Avoid recommenders who ask the student to write their own letter for them to sign - these letters tend to sound repetitive and less authentic
When choosing between recommenders, prefer the stronger storyteller, regardless of subject taught

Ask for recommendations via email rather than in person, giving at least two weeks' notice, and provide a resume/activity list, essay drafts or outlines, specific themes to emphasize, and target schools/majors
Follow up close to the deadline with a gentle reminder, send a thank-you after submission, and report back with the outcome once decisions are in
notable_or_distinctive: Provides an unusually detailed, step-by-step recommender request/follow-up process (email templates, what materials to send, timing of reminders) rather than just general selection advice.
reliability_notes: Generally sound, practical advice reflecting standard counselor guidance; some claims (e.g., checkbox-style rating questionnaires teachers fill out) are plausible but not universally verified across all schools; older video (6 years) so some platform-specific details may be dated.
